what: Dev-only comparison of the four segmenters the live engine could run, each at its own profile (drishyam.agent.PROFILES) and charged its own cost table: the dacl10k v2a and v2b ONNX models, the dacl10k v1 ONNX model and the classical engine. Never a held-out set. Pre-registration stub: the criterion below was committed while v2b's grid was running and before any v2b row existed; v2a's and v1's dev rows had been read. The rows, the pairs and the recommendation are added after.
criterion: Recall at the 30 % cap (JobConfig's default) on CODEBRIM dev100 (real photos) and on synth_dev. Model A is better than model B on a split when the paired 95 % bootstrap CI of A's recall ratio to B (images resampled together, evals.harness.boot_ci) lies wholly above 1, worse when it lies wholly below 1; a CI that touches or crosses 1 is no measurable difference. On the clean dev split at the 30 % cap A harms against B when the paired CI of A's boxes-per-photo difference to B, or of its difference in the share of photos with any box, lies wholly above 0, by the same standard. A model is best on dev when, against each of the other three, it is better on at least one recall split, worse on neither and has no clean harm. If no model qualifies, none is best on dev by this standard, and the pairs say where each wins and loses. Modelled ms per job, the 1.0 cap, IoU-only recall, critical boxes and the ratios to L0 tiling and the downscale are reported, not part of the criterion; ms from cost tables timed at different machine loads are not comparable between models (each table's load is listed).
